evidence.title: Pricing page truthfulness: photos sold as included (MMS is a $5 module), module ledger missing, voice denied
evidence.body:
**Severity:** P1 — fix before launch
**Found by:** bughunt/bug-drift, ux-polish/ux-marketing, marketing/mkt-claims, marketing/mkt-strengths · confirmed by adversarial verifier

Four auditors independently confirmed the pricing page contradicts the shipped #12 module model. Three distinct fixes on the same page: (1) stop advertising outbound photos as included in every plan — MMS is a $5/mo opt-in module hard-capped at 150/mo; (2) the "That's the whole list" cost ledger must list the $5/$8 module add-on prices; (3) stop denying voice — call forwarding + missed-call text-back ship as the $8 voice module.

**Where:** `apps/web/src/app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx:84`

**Evidence:** Pricing page lists "Photos you send: count as 3 texts" as a feature of BOTH plans (lines 84, 102) and the FAQ answers "How do photo messages count?" with "Sending a photo counts as three texts from your allowance" (line 256), with zero mention of the module. Same claim on apps/web/src/app/(marketing)/features/shared-inbox/page.tsx:236 ("Loonext handles SMS and MMS to and from your business number") and for/landscapers/page.tsx:158 ("Photos in and out"), and apps/web/public/llms.txt:16,29 ("Sending a photo counts as three texts", "Photos both ways (MMS)"). But the API hard-gates outbound MMS behind the opt-in $5/mo "Picture messages" module: apps/api/src/routes/compose.ts:349-354 throws 409 conflict ("Sending pictures needs the Picture messages add-on") when isModuleEnabled(db, companyId, "mms") is false, mirrored in apps/api/src/routes/messages.ts; the module costs 500 cents/mo and is capped at 150/mo (apps/api/src/billing/modules.ts:52-61, plans.ts:76-79). Only pre-migration companies are grandfathered (supabase/migrations/20260704160000_company_modules.sql:28-30) — every NEW signup the marketing site targets must buy the add-on.

**Impact:** A new customer pays $29 expecting to text photos (the plumber/landscaper pages sell photo workflows as the core use case), then gets a 409 upsell on their first picture send. That is a false pricing claim on the page the site calls its transparency centerpiece — chargeback/refund fuel and a direct contradiction of the 'see the price, pay, start texting' positioning.

**Recommended fix:** Either add the module lineup ($5 Picture messages / $8 Call forwarding / $5 Extra storage) to the pricing page and reword the plan cards to "Photos you send (with the Picture messages add-on): count as 3 texts", or fold outbound MMS into the base plans. Update shared-inbox, landscapers/plumbers/hvac trade pages, the pricing FAQ, and llms.txt in the same pass.

<details><summary>Adversarial verification (confirmed)</summary>

Independently reproduced every leg of the finding. (1) Marketing claims: apps/web/src/app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx lists "Photos you send: count as 3 texts" in BOTH plan cards (lines 84, 102) and the FAQ answers "How do photo messages count?" with "Sending a photo counts as three texts from your allowance" (line 256); a grep for "add-on|module|Picture messages" across the whole pricing page returns zero matches — the module lineup is never disclosed. Same claims verified at apps/web/src/app/(marketing)/features/shared-inbox/page.tsx:236 ("Loonext handles SMS and MMS to and from your business number"), for/landscapers/page.tsx:158 ("Photos in and out...") and :165 ("photos count as three"), and apps/web/public/llms.txt:16,29. (2) API hard gate: apps/api/src/routes/compose.ts:349-354 throws a 409 ("Sending pictures needs the Picture messages add-on — turn it on in Settings › Billing.") when isModuleEnabled(db, companyId, "mms") is false; the check is commented as MANDATORY cost-protection. isModuleEnabled (apps/api/src/billing/company-modules.ts:17-33) returns true only when a company_modules row exists with disabled_at IS NULL. (3) New signups do NOT get MMS: supabase/migrations/20260704160000_company_modules.sql:28-30 seeds 'mms' only for companies existing at migration time (explicit GRANDFATHERING comment); the only enablement paths afterward are paid — Stripe checkout line items (apps/api/src/routes/billing.ts:184-198, enablement written on checkout.completed per apps/api/src/webhooks/stripe.ts:266-274) and the paid POST /v1/billing/modules toggle (billing.ts:461+). The onboarding plan builder defaults to zero modules selected (apps/web/src/app/onboarding/plan/page.tsx:86, useState<PlanModule[]>([]) with the comment "opt-in add-ons carried into checkout"). (4) Not an intentional documented exception: docs/DECISIONS.md and docs/PRICING-AUDIT.md document the #12 module model and cost gating but say nothing blessing the marketing pages' unqualified photo claims. So a new $29 customer who follows the pricing page's promise gets a 409 upsell on their first outbound photo — the impact as reported is real. P1 is appropriate (false pricing claim / refund risk, not a security or availability P0).

</details>

---

**Where:** `apps/web/src/app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx:84`

**Evidence:** Both plan cards state "Photos you send: count as 3 texts" (lines 84, 102) and the FAQ answers "Sending a photo counts as three texts from your allowance" (lines 255-256). The actual product gates MMS sending on the paid "Picture messages" module ($5/mo, apps/web/src/lib/api/types.ts:743-750): apps/api/src/routes/compose.ts:349 and routes/messages.ts:221 reject media when the module is off, apps/api/src/billing/plans.ts:76-79 caps it at 150 outbound MMS/month flat, and messaging/send.ts:350-351 strips media past the cap. Photos do NOT count as segments at all (send.ts:257-259: "no MMS segment estimate, no photo segment count"). The same stale copy also survives in-app at apps/web/src/app/(app)/settings/usage/page.tsx:453.

**Impact:** A customer buys on the advertised "photos = 3 texts" model, then discovers photo sending is blocked entirely until they add a $5/mo module capped at 150 — a false advertising claim on the exact page whose brand promise is total price honesty, and a refund/chargeback/trust risk in week one.

**Recommended fix:** Rewrite the two plan-card bullets and the photo FAQ to describe the real model: sending photos requires the Picture messages add-on, $5/mo with 150 included, incoming photos always free. Update settings/usage/page.tsx:453 to match.

<details><summary>Adversarial verification (confirmed)</summary>

Pricing page still advertises "Photos you send: count as 3 texts" (apps/web/src/app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx:84,102) and FAQ "counts as three texts" (:256), plus in-app apps/web/src/app/(app)/settings/usage/page.tsx:453 — but the shipped product gates photo sending behind the opt-in $5/mo "Picture messages" module (apps/api/src/routes/compose.ts:349-354 throws 409 when module off; isModuleEnabled is default-off, apps/api/src/billing/company-modules.ts:17-33), caps it flat at 150/mo (apps/api/src/billing/plans.ts:76-79) with cap-and-drop media stripping (apps/api/src/messaging/send.ts:344-365), and photos no longer consume text segments (send.ts:257-259 "no MMS segment estimate"). Also apps/web/src/app/(marketing)/for/plumbers/page.tsx:190 ("Photos count as three each") has the same stale claim. docs/DECISIONS.md D5's "MMS meters as 3 segments" predates the #12 module model the code implements; no decision sanctions keeping the old copy. False-advertising/chargeback impact is real.

</details>

---

**Where:** `apps/web/src/app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx:84`

**Evidence:** Both plan cards list "Photos you send: count as 3 texts" as an included feature (pricing/page.tsx:84 and :102), and the FAQ at :256 says "Sending a photo counts as three texts" with overage at 3¢. Shipped reality: MMS sending is gated behind the opt-in $5/mo "Picture messages" module (apps/api/src/routes/compose.ts:349 and routes/messages.ts:221 return 409 when the module is off; apps/api/src/billing/modules.ts:52-61 prices it at 500 cents), the onboarding plan builder defaults modules to [] (apps/web/src/app/onboarding/plan/page.tsx:86), and even with the module on, sends are hard-capped at 150 outbound MMS per period after which media is silently STRIPPED and the message goes out text-only (apps/api/src/messaging/send.ts:265-296 and :312-318, apps/api/src/billing/plans.ts:76-79). llms.txt:16/:29 and docs/marketing/COPY.md:450/:462 repeat the same stale claim.

**Impact:** A buyer who signs up specifically to text job photos (the exact use case the trade pages sell) finds photo sending disabled unless they pay $5/mo more, and even then their 151st photo of the month silently degrades to text-only — a concrete false-advertising/refund-request generator on the page whose headline is "Nothing hidden."

**Recommended fix:** On the pricing page (and llms.txt + COPY.md §PR), move photo sending out of the base-plan feature lists and state it as the "Picture messages" add-on: $5/mo, 150 outbound picture messages included, receiving always free; disclose the cap-and-drop behavior in the photo FAQ.

<details><summary>Adversarial verification (confirmed)</summary>

pricing/page.tsx:84,:102 list "Photos you send: count as 3 texts" as included base-plan features and FAQ :255-256 repeats it, with no mention anywhere on the page of the add-on, its $5/mo price, or the cap (grep for MMS/picture/add-on finds nothing else). Meanwhile compose.ts:349-354 409s picture sends unless the "mms" module is enabled ("Sending pictures needs the Picture messages add-on"), modules.ts:52-61 prices that module at 500 cents/mo, plans.ts:76-79 caps included outbound MMS at 150/period for both plans, and send.ts:265-296 + :312-318 strip media (text-only degrade) once over cap or with the module off. The module gating is the intentional #12 design (modules.ts header), so the marketing copy is the stale side — the mismatch and false-advertising impact are real.

</details>

---

**Where:** `apps/web/src/app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx:84`

**Evidence:** Pricing page plan cards list "Photos you send: count as 3 texts" on both Starter (line 84) and Pro (line 102), and the FAQ says "Sending a photo counts as three texts from your allowance" (line 256) with no mention of the module. Same claim on /for/contractors (page.tsx:225 "photos of progress count as three") and /for/hvac (page.tsx:166), and in apps/web/public/llms.txt:16. Product truth: sending MMS requires the $5/mo "Picture messages" module (apps/api/src/billing/modules.ts:52-61 — gates: "sending picture (MMS) messages") and is hard-capped at 150/mo with cap-and-drop and no overage (apps/api/src/billing/plans.ts:59-79).

**Impact:** A buyer who signs up expecting to text job photos on the $29 plan (the HVAC and contractor pages sell photo triage as a core workflow) hits a paywall in compose, discovers a $5/mo add-on and a 150/photo cap never disclosed anywhere on the marketing site — a false billing claim on the brand whose entire pitch is "every cost, before you pay."

**Recommended fix:** Update the plan-card line and FAQ on /pricing, the trade-page pricing blurbs, and llms.txt to the module truth: e.g. "Add picture messaging for $5/mo — 150 photos a month included; each also counts as 3 texts. Receiving photos is always free." Keep the 3-text metering sentence only alongside the module disclosure.

<details><summary>Adversarial verification (confirmed)</summary>

Marketing copy sells base-plan photo sending (apps/web/src/app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx:84,102,256; for/contractors/page.tsx:225; for/hvac/page.tsx:166; public/llms.txt:16,29) with zero mention of the MMS module — grep of the pricing page for MMS/picture/module finds nothing. Product code gates sending behind the $5/mo mms module (apps/api/src/billing/modules.ts:52-61) with a 150/mo hard cap (apps/api/src/billing/plans.ts:76-79), enforced at the send choke point: apps/api/src/messaging/send.ts:272 returns over-cap when isModuleEnabled(db, companyId, "mms") is false and lines 344-350 strip media. No DECISIONS.md entry sanctions the discrepancy — DECISIONS.md:92 still describes the pre-module "MMS meters as 3 segments" model, predating commit 2b71ed7 that added the module gate; the marketing copy is stale, not intentional.

</details>

---

**Where:** `apps/web/src/app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx:189`

**Evidence:** The honesty ledger closes with "That's the whole list. No setup fees, no per-user fees..." (lines 189-192) and the hero promises "every cost on this page" (line 302). The product now sells four opt-in modules the page never mentions: mms $5, voice $8, extra_storage $5, regions_ca $5 (apps/api/src/billing/modules.ts:23-89; card copy in apps/web/src/lib/api/types.ts:743-771; picked in onboarding at apps/web/src/app/onboarding/plan/page.tsx:86-123 and in-app at components/settings/plan-modules-card.tsx). The FAQ also answers "Loonext... doesn't do voice calls" (line 276) while the product sells an $8/mo call-forwarding + missed-call-text-back module (companies.ts:241 gates it) that no marketing page mentions.

**Impact:** The anti-Podium positioning (every cost published, no surprises) is broken the moment a buyer reaches the in-app or onboarding plan builder and finds four monthly add-ons the pricing page said didn't exist; the voice FAQ also talks a buyer out of a feature the product actually sells.

**Recommended fix:** Add a compact "Add-ons" strip to /pricing mirroring PLAN_MODULE_CARDS ($5 pictures/150, $8 call forwarding/300 min, $5 storage/10GB, $5 Canada numbers), amend the "whole list" ledger row to include them, and reword the voice FAQ to mention call forwarding + missed-call text-back.

<details><summary>Adversarial verification (confirmed)</summary>

pricing/page.tsx:189-191 states "That's the whole list" and :276 "doesn't do voice calls", yet apps/api/src/billing/modules.ts:51-90 defines four paid opt-in modules (mms $5, voice $8, extra_storage $5, regions_ca $5) that buyers are shown and charged for via onboarding/plan/page.tsx:86-123,229-238 and components/settings/plan-modules-card.tsx (card copy in lib/api/types.ts:743-771). Grep of the entire (marketing) tree and marketing components finds zero mention of any module; docs/DECISIONS.md documents no decision to omit them (its only related line, "No per-seat add-ons in MVP" at line 90, is itself contradicted by the shipped #12 plan builder). No DB constraint, middleware, or documented decision makes the gap not real.

</details>

---

**Where:** `apps/web/src/app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx:189`

**Evidence:** The honesty ledger's closing row (pricing/page.tsx:189-192) claims "That's the whole list. No setup fees, no per-user fees..." and the hero (:301-303) promises "every cost on this page." But checkout's plan builder sells four paid add-ons the page never mentions: Picture messages $5/mo, Call forwarding $8/mo, Extra storage $5/mo (apps/web/src/lib/api/types.ts:743-770 PLAN_MODULE_CARDS, rendered by apps/web/src/app/onboarding/plan/page.tsx:227-229 and settings/plan-modules-card.tsx). No marketing page mentions any module (repo-wide grep of (marketing) for "Picture messages"/"add-on"/"$5" finds only competitor pricing).

**Impact:** The trust centerpiece of the anti-Podium positioning ("every cost, before you pay") is factually incomplete the moment a buyer reaches /onboarding/plan and sees $5-$8/mo toggles that were never disclosed — exactly the hidden-fee pattern the page attacks competitors for.

**Recommended fix:** Add an "Optional add-ons" block to the pricing page (and COPY.md §PR) listing the three visible modules with their prices and included quantities, and soften "That's the whole list" to cover base plans + these optional add-ons.

<details><summary>Adversarial verification (confirmed)</summary>

Independently reproduced. The pricing page's honesty ledger claims completeness ("That's the whole list. No setup fees, no per-user fees..." — apps/web/src/app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx:189-192) and the hero promises "every cost on this page" (:301-303), yet the checkout plan builder sells paid add-ons never mentioned there: PLAN_MODULE_CARDS in apps/web/src/lib/api/types.ts:743-771 defines Picture messages $5/mo, Call forwarding $8/mo, Extra storage $5/mo (regions_ca $5 is filtered out as inert), and apps/web/src/app/onboarding/plan/page.tsx:218-269 renders the three toggles with "{mod.price}/mo" directly on the pre-checkout screen. A grep of apps/web/src/app/(marketing) for "Picture messages|Call forwarding|Extra storage|add-on" finds only competitor-pricing mentions — no Loonext add-on is disclosed on any marketing page. Not enforced/excused elsewhere: docs/DECISIONS.md has no entry deferring or intentionally omitting module disclosure from marketing (D4/Reviews removals are unrelated), and docs/PRICING-AUDIT.md (#12, "COMPLETE") documents shipping the plan builder with no marketing-copy follow-up. The staleness goes further than the auditor noted: the pricing FAQ still says Loonext "doesn't do voice calls" (page.tsx:276) while checkout sells a Call forwarding module, and the plan cards state "Photos you send: count as 3 texts" (:86, :102) with no mention that MMS is a $5/mo module — so the page is not merely incomplete but contradicts the shipped plan model. P1 severity is apt for a trust-positioning product pre-deploy.

</details>

---

**Where:** `apps/web/src/app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx:189`

**Evidence:** The honesty ledger's closing item reads "That's the whole list. No setup fees, no per-user fees, no monthly 'compliance' or 'carrier' line items" (lines 189-192), enumerating plan price, $29 registration, overage, and tax only. The product also sells recurring monthly add-ons: mms $5/mo, voice $8/mo, extra_storage $5/mo (apps/api/src/billing/modules.ts:51-90), which onboarding offers before first payment (apps/web/src/app/onboarding/plan/page.tsx:229).

**Impact:** The trust centerpiece of the whole site makes an exhaustiveness claim that a buyer can falsify five minutes later at the onboarding plan step, where three optional monthly line items appear — the exact 'gotcha' pattern the page attacks competitors for.

**Recommended fix:** Add a ledger row: "Optional add-ons — picture messages $5/mo, call forwarding $8/mo, extra storage $5/mo. Off by default; you turn them on, you can turn them off." Keep "that's the whole list" as the row after it.

<details><summary>Adversarial verification (confirmed)</summary>

apps/web/src/app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx:168-193 — the LEDGER array lists only plan/$29 registration/extra texts/tax and closes with "That's the whole list… no monthly 'compliance' or 'carrier' line items"; no add-on row exists and grep finds no add-on/module mention anywhere in pricing/page.tsx. Meanwhile apps/api/src/billing/modules.ts:51-90 defines recurring monthly add-ons (mms 500¢, voice 800¢, extra_storage 500¢, regions_ca 500¢) with Stripe licensed prices, and apps/web/src/app/onboarding/plan/page.tsx:218-263 renders them as an "Add-ons" section with "{mod.price}/mo" rows that ride into checkout (line 123) before first payment. docs/DECISIONS.md has no decision sanctioning the omission — line 90's "No per-seat add-ons in MVP" is about seats, not modules; D4 concerns the footer. The add-ons are opt-in/off-by-default, which mitigates but does not refute the exhaustiveness claim being false.

</details>

---

**Where:** `apps/web/src/app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx:276`

**Evidence:** Pricing FAQ: "it doesn't do voice calls" (line 276). /compare/quo repeats it categorically: "Loonext can't call anyone" (page.tsx:248) and "Not included. Loonext can't make calls" (page.tsx:92). Product truth: the $8/mo voice module forwards calls from the business number to a cell with 300 min/mo included (apps/api/src/billing/modules.ts:62-71), and missed-call text-back is a shipped settings feature (apps/web/src/app/(app)/settings/missed-calls/page.tsx:98 "Text back a missed call").

**Impact:** Missed-call text-back is the feature Podium built its category on and a top objection for this ICP ("what happens when they call the texting number?"); the site answers "nothing," conceding buyers to Quo unnecessarily and contradicting what onboarding then sells them. It's true Loonext can't place calls, but 'can't call anyone / doesn't do voice' overstates the gap.

**Recommended fix:** Reword to the precise truth everywhere voice is denied: "Loonext doesn't make calls — but calls to your number forward to your cell (optional $8/mo, 300 minutes), and missed calls get an automatic text-back so the lead lands in your inbox." Add missed-call text-back to the compare/quo voice row and consider a homepage feature-card mention.

<details><summary>Adversarial verification (confirmed)</summary>

Marketing denials verified verbatim: pricing/page.tsx:276 "doesn't do voice calls"; compare/quo/page.tsx:92 "Loonext can't make calls", :248 "Loonext can't call anyone", :363 "cannot place or receive a call" (the last is flatly false). Product ships the contradicting features: apps/api/src/billing/modules.ts:61-70 voice module ("Forward calls from your business number to your cell, and text back the ones you miss", 800 cents/mo) with 300 min/mo (apps/api/src/billing/plans.ts:53-56), and the missed-call text-back settings page at apps/web/src/app/(app)/settings/missed-calls/page.tsx:98. docs/DECISIONS.md D26 (line 747) documents the shipped voice wave; no decision marks the marketing denial as intentional, and grep confirms neither marketing page mentions forwarding/modules/$8 anywhere. Repo convention (DECISIONS.md line 415) is to flip marketing copy when capability ships, which was not done here.

</details>

_Filed by the `loonext-launch-audit` agent team (run `wf_241dc0ca-b6d`, 2026-07-07)._
